official.title: Research Assistant (master thesis worker), information theory
official.description_text:
Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 16 000 students and 5 200 employees, including 446 professors. Our campus is in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland.  Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.
The Information Theory research team at Aalto University (Department of Information and Communications Engineering, School of Electrical Engineering) invites applications for a 6-month
Research Assistant position for master thesis worker
.
About the team
We work across discrete mathematics and information theory, including
coding theory, combinatorial algorithms, design theory, and graph theory.
Computational methods are central; the team operates a 500‑core cluster.
We both compete with and leverage AI; see:
https://www.aalto.fi/en/news/researcher-cracks-new-kissing-number-bounds-besting-ai-in-the-process
Project focus
One class of structures we study is Hadamard matrices — orthogonal combinatorial objects with applications in quantum technology. In this position, you will develop and implement computational methods to investigate how a technique called switching transforms various types of Hadamard matrices.
Qualifications
Background in mathematics or computer science
Excellent programming skills and experience with C
Interest in computational discrete mathematics and algorithmic experimentation
NOTE!
This position is open only for Aalto University students.
What we offer
Paid employment for master's thesis work (salary: 2622 €/month).
The position is fixed term from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027.
How to apply
To apply, please submit your application through our recruitment site ("Apply now!” at the bottom of the page) as soon as possible and no later than on 24 Sep 2026.
Please include the following attachments to your application:
CV
Transcript of study records
Brief motivation letter
Please note: Aalto University employees should apply for the position via our internal HR system, Workday (Internal Jobs), using their existing Workday user account (not the external webpage for open positions). If you are a student or visitor at Aalto University, please apply with your personal email address (not aalto.fi) via
Aalto University open positions
For more information about the position, please contact Professor Patric Östergård (patric.ostergard@aalto.fi;
https://users.aalto.fi/pat/
). Yhteydenotossa voit myös käyttää suomea. Vid kontakt kan du också använda svenska.
For questions about the application process, please contact HR Advisor Johanna Haapalainen at hr-elec@aalto.fi.

ai.summary: 6-month research assistant position for Aalto University master's students in the Information Theory research team (Department of Information and Communications Engineering). Focus is computational methods for investigating Hadamard matrices and switching transformations, leveraging the team's 500-core computing cluster.

thematic_fit.rationale: Pure discrete mathematics and information theory (coding theory, combinatorial algorithms, graph theory, Hadamard matrices). No connection to immersive systems, spatial cognition, learning, collaboration, or human factors. Core research is computational mathematics, not HCI or XR.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position emphasizes computational discrete mathematics and algorithm development. Researcher's expertise is in design science, user-centred evaluation, experimental HCI methods, and collaborative system design. Negligible methodological alignment. The requirement for strong C programming skills differs from researcher's Unity/C# experience.

growth_value.rationale: Computational mathematics skill development does not close identified gaps (eye-tracking, physiological sensing, statistics, mixed-effects modelling) nor advance immersive systems research. Would be a distraction from building a cohesive HCI research portfolio.

strategic_value.rationale: Position is open only to Aalto University students; researcher is enrolled at Multimedia University (Malaysia), not Aalto. Ineligible. Even if eligible, Information Theory group operates in pure mathematics, not HCI. No strategic value for target identity.

eligibility_flags: Position explicitly restricted to Aalto University students only. Researcher is currently enrolled at Multimedia University (MMU), Malaysia. Ineligible.
risks: Researcher is ineligible: position restricted to Aalto students; researcher is at MMU.
Even if eligibility could be clarified, disciplinary mismatch is severe: pure mathematics vs. HCI.
No relevance to immersive systems, spatial cognition, or human-centred research.
Short duration (6 months) and research focus (Hadamard matrices) would not contribute to HCI research portfolio or target career trajectory.

eligibility_reasons: funding/salary not confirmed on the posting
